observations.title: Jane McDonald
observations.description: National treasure, singing sensation and local lass Jane McDonald is coming back to her home county of Yorkshire in 2026 on her ‘Living The Dream’ UK tour, returning to Leeds for the 5th time to close her tour right here at first direct bank arena.In support of the tour, Jane will release her new album Living The Dream next spring. Jane recorded the album in Nashville at the famous Blackbird Studios. Living The Dream is Jane’s 11th studio album and presents her nod to Country.Making the announcement, Jane said: “It’s true, I am officially Living The Dream so what better way to celebrate that than with a new album and a new tour.Whether you’ve seen Jane McDonald live before or this will be your first time, this is one you do not want to miss. Join us for an evening full of new material and classic hits.  Make sure you’re in Leeds to experience it!

observations.description: After performing his smash-hit show ‘Horizons’ to nearly half a million people across the world, Professor Brian Cox is back with his new tour world tour Emergence, coming to first direct bank arena on 10 October, 2026. Brian has appeared in many landmark science programs for BBC radio and television over the last 15 years, from the Peabody Award-winning Wonders of the Solar System, The Planets and the exceptionally funny, The Infinite Monkey Cage. Professor Brian Cox creates a jaw dropping gaze into the wonderous journey through space and time, don't miss this magical and mind blowing show.

observations.title: The Rock Orchestra
observations.description: Get ready, Leeds! The Rock Orchestra – Arena of Fire is coming to the first direct bank arena on 1 October 2026 for a spectacular night of music that rock fans won’t want to miss. Blending the raw power of rock and metal with the sweeping drama of a symphony, The Rock Orchestra experience is a unique live show that has captivated audiences across the world.This isn't just another concert - it’s an unforgettable celebration of legendary rock and metal anthems reimagined through a breath-taking orchestral lens. With an ensemble of world-class classical musicians performing iconic songs from artists such as Metallica, AC/DC, Guns N’ Roses, Nirvana, Linkin Park and more, The Rock Orchestra delivers a powerful fusion of styles that resonates with both rock devotees and newcomers alike.Disclaimer: The Rock Orchestra and its events are not affiliated with the artists and composers listed. All trademarks are the property of their respective owners.

observations.title: The World of Hans Zimmer
observations.description: As musical director and curator, the master Hans Zimmer, is largely responsible for The World of Hans Zimmer show, even when he is not onstage himself.Captivating, overwhelming and fantastically cinematic, The World of Hans Zimmer is a top-class show highlight and a real treat for fans. Zimmer’s unique new orchestral suites will be combined with visually stunning projections, powerful sound arrangements and moving solo performances to create an unforgettable experience for all the senses.Matt Dunkley conjures the magic of Hans Zimmer’s works live on stage for this upcoming arena tour. Dunkley is a world-leading orchestrator, arranger and conductor with an impressive musical career closely linked to the world of cinema. His long-standing professional partnership with Hans Zimmer is reflected in their collaboration on blockbuster films such as the third and fourth ‘Pirates of the Caribbean’ movies, ‘Inception,’ ‘The Dark Knight,’ ‘The Dark Knight Rises,’ James Bond ‘No Time To Die,’ ‘Kung Fu Panda 3’ and ‘Top Gun: Maverick.’

observations.title: Diwali Story — A Musical
observations.description: One night. One stage. The greatest story in Indian culture — told at the biggest scale it has ever been seen.Following a sold-out debut at the Royal Albert Hall, Diwali Story returns in a bold new production — brand new music, new songs, and a full retelling of the Musical Story of Ram and the celebration of Diwali, performed in English and designed for a new generation of audiences. Diwali is the festival of lights. But at its heart, it has always been a story — the story of Lord Ram: his exile, his courage, his battle against darkness, and his triumphant return that lit a thousand lamps and gave the world Diwali. For one night at OVO Arena Wembley, that story comes alive in its most spectacular form yet. Diwali Story is a full-scale community celebration — live music, live dance, and live theatre brought together on the biggest stage in Britain, in front of thousands of people. More than 15 choreographed dances. 16 original songs. Stunning stage and screen visuals that bring the legend of Diwali to life in a way you have never seen before. This is not a concert and it is not a dance show. It is the complete Diwali experience — the colour, the joy, the devotion, and the triumph. Come ready to sing. Every ticket purchased directly supports the celebration and preservation of India's sacred cultural heritage for future generations. Diwali Story is presented by Sanatan Events CIC, a community interest company dedicated to bringing India's greatest cultural stories to the largest possible stages.

observations.title: Simple Plan
observations.description: For more than two decades, SIMPLE PLAN has been one of the most culturally and commercially successful bands in rock. Their multi-platinum 2002 debut album, No Pads, No Helmets… Just Balls bore the smash singles “I’d Do Anything,” “I’m Just A Kid,” “Addicted” and “Perfect,” while subsequent hits “Welcome To My Life,” “Summer Paradise,” “Untitled (How Could This Happen To Me?),” “Shut Up!” and “What’s New Scooby-Doo?” have cemented their legacy as pop-punk legends. In all, the Montreal-formed quartet has sold over 10 million albums worldwide, captivated the main stages of the Vans Warped Tour and When We Were Young, performed at the 2010 Winter Olympics and with the Montreal Symphony Orchestra, sold out shows around the world and raised more than $3 million through the Simple Plan Foundation. Their videos have garnered more than a billion YouTube views, while their inescapable social media presence driven another billion views on the viral #ImJustAKid Challenge alongside videos from *NSYNC, Ed Sheeran, and Venus and Serena Williams. In 2025, they’ll celebrate their landmark 25th anniversary with their biggest year yet, anchored by a career-spanning documentary on Amazon Prime Video, worldwide amphitheater and arena tours with Avril Lavigne and The Offspring and their most ambitious headlining trek in 20 years, the Bigger Than You Think! tour.

observations.title: Rockbourne Fair 14-16 October 2026
observations.description: <p>We’re excited for the return of Rockbourne Fair this October, all in support of the Stars Appeal, Salisbury Hospital’s Charity.</p> <p>The 3-day shopping event, organised by the Rockbourne Fair Committee,<strong> </strong>runs from Wednesday 14th to Friday 16th October at Salisbury Racecourse. The Fair will stay open until 7.30pm on the Thursday evening, offering visitors the chance to enjoy late-night shopping.</p> <p><strong>Event Details:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Wednesday 14th October: 10am – 5pm</li> <li>Thursday 15th October: 10am – 7.30pm (<em>Late-Night Shopping</em>)</li> <li>Friday 16th October: 10am – 3pm</li> </ul> <p><strong>Venue:</strong> Salisbury Racecourse, SP2 8PN</p> <p><strong>Entry:</strong> £6 per person (<em>Special £3 entry after 6pm on Thursday</em>)</p> <p><strong>Free parking available</strong></p> <p>With over 90 handpicked stalls packed with fashion, jewellery, homeware, cosmetics, gourmet food, and unique gifts there is plenty on offer for visitors searching for their perfect Christmas gift, many of which cannot be found on the high street. This year, the Fair has over 30 new stalls.</p> <p>The money raised will help the Stars Appeal towards the £2million it aims to raise this year to fund projects across Salisbury Hospital. These include new equipment such as a mammogram machine for the Breast Unit, enhancements to buildings, and ongoing projects across the hospital, including support for people with cancer, a dedicated play assistant on the Children’s Unit, and Stars Appeal Wi-Fi.</p> <p>Last year, Rockbourne Fair raised a record-breaking total of £68,191, surpassing the £62,081 raised in 2024.</p> <p>Also returning to the event is the popular Rockbourne Fair Lunch Menu, available in the on-site restaurant, offering seasonal dishes, coffee and cake deals, and even a glass of fizz for those in the festive spirit. Wood-fired sourdough pizzas will also be available to enjoy al fresco during the Fair.</p> <p>For more information visit <a href="http://www.rockbournefair.org.uk">www.rockbournefair.org.uk</a></p> <p> </p> <p> </p> <p> </p> <table style="height: 5px;" width="5"> <tbody> <tr> <td width="600"></td> </tr> </tbody> </table>

observations.title: Salisbury Fireworks 2026
observations.description: <p>Join us for Salisbury’s biggest fireworks night!</p> <p>It will be an evening packed with fun, with <a href="https://www.salisburyradio.co.uk/">Salisbury Radio</a> keeping us entertained with a kids’ disco followed by the ultimate 80’s & 90’s throwbacks. Our bars will be fully stocked and there are several local food units with an array of food choices on offer.</p> <p>We’re also thrilled to be supporting <a href="https://www.salisburyhospicecharity.org.uk/">Salisbury Hospice</a> once again, helping to raise vital funds to continue providing essential care and support to patients and their families across Wiltshire and parts of Hampshire and Dorset.</p> <p><strong>What’s On</strong></p> <p>5.30pm Gates open</p> <p>6.15pm – 7.00pm Kids’ Disco with Salisbury Radio</p> <p>7.00pm – 7.30pm 80s & 90s Throwbacks with Salisbury Radio</p> <p>7.30 – 7.45pm The Fireworks Display!</p> <p>7.45 – 8:30pm 80s & 90s Throwbacks with Salisbury Radio</p> <p>Food units and bars close at 8.00pm.</p> <p><strong>Getting Here</strong></p> <p>Our fireworks night is expected to be an extremely busy event, so please allow plenty of extra time for your journey to and from the racecourse. Food outlets and bars will remain open until 8.00pm, with music continuing until 8.30pm, so stay a little longer to enjoy the entertainment.</p> <p><strong>Parking</strong></p> <p>All car parking needs to be prebooked with your tickets, as parking is limited. If you are familiar with the site, please do not attempt to head to a specific car park, please follow instructions by the car parking stewards who will park you as quickly and efficiently as possible.</p> <p><em>If you have not purchased a parking space with your tickets, you will need to come via our park & ride service from Wilton Park & Ride.</em></p> <p>If you require accessible parking, please inform the car parking steward when you arrive and clearly display your Blue Badge on the dashboard.</p> <p><strong>Park & Ride</strong></p> <p>Park & Ride buses will depart from Wilton Park & Ride every 15 minutes from 5.00pm until 7.00pm. Buses will then depart from the racecourse every 15 minutes from 8.00pm until 9.00pm.</p> <p>The full timetable can be found <a class="" href="https://www.salisburyracecourse.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Salisbury-Reds-Fireworks-Timetable-2026.pdf">HERE</a><strong>. </strong></p> <p><strong>Food & Drink</strong></p> <p>There will be a fantastic selection of local food units serving a variety of delicious options, including: Greek Gringo, Chicken Gringo, Bratwurst, Toasties, Pizza’s & Jacket potatoes.</p> <p>Our bars will also be fully stocked and open until 8pm, with alcoholic, soft and hot drinks available.</p> <p>Don’t miss Salisbury’s biggest fireworks night! Tickets are limited, so buy yours now before they sell out!</p> <p><!--Future Ticketing API - START--><br /> <script type='text/javascript' src='https://embed.futureticketing.ie/ft6141a3569515b'></script><br /> <script type='text/javascript'>var FTicket = FT({FT_event:'101'});</script><br /> <!--Future Ticketing API - END--></p>

observations.title: Season Finale
observations.description: <p><strong>Event Summary:</strong>  The season finale and a race day which traditionally features plenty of 2 year old horses as they venture onto a racecourse for the very first time.</p> <p>Gates open at midday the first race is at 2:04pm and the last race at 4:55pm.</p> <p><strong>Children:</strong>  Accompanied children aged under 17 and under get in FREE at all Salisbury race days, however, no additional facilities for children are provided at this fixture.</p> <p><strong>1584 Restaurant & Conservatory: </strong>Our two restaurants offer guests a relaxed, sociable way to enjoy the day with a reserved table for the entire race meeting. Our 1584 Restaurant & Conservatory provide the choice of a traditional carvery (vegetarian option available as main course) or a cold chef’s buffet table, making it ideal for groups or those looking for a more leisurely raceday experience. Packages start from £108 per person (£115 for Saturday evenings) and include admission and a racecard. While there is no direct view of the course from the restaurants, you are only steps away from the Bibury Lawn, where you can stand and watch the racing by the winning post. Restaurant bookings are sold as part of a combined admission and dining ticket and are therefore subject to our Terms & Conditions and are non-refundable. Click here to see our sample menu <a href="https://www.salisburyracecourse.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/2026-carvery-Menu.pdf">2026 carvery Menu</a></p> <p><strong>Bars & Food Outlets:</strong>   Each enclosure has access to bars and catering, including mobile food units.   Own food i.e. picnics (but not to include any alcohol) can be brought into the Sarum Enclosure ONLY, on any race day.</p> <p><strong>Car Parking:</strong>  All car parking at Salisbury Racecourse is FREE and each car park is located just a short distance from the enclosures.</p> <p><strong>Complimentary Bus Service</strong>:  More details to follow in due course.</p> <p><strong>Big screen:  </strong>There are <strong>two</strong> big screens. The 25 metre square screen will be located opposite the parade ring and the 100 metre square screen will be facing the enclosures, about half a furlong from the winning post.  The big screens are provided by a contractor.  Salisbury Racecourse is not liable in the event of a picture failure to a screen during a race meeting, or if for any reason a screen fails to make it to the racecourse.</p> <p><strong>Assistance Dogs</strong>: Are welcome with the relevant paperwork.</p> <p><strong>Equine safety & welfare</strong>: British horse racing’s hub dedicated to the Thoroughbred racehorse is <a href="https://horsepwr.co.uk/">https://horsepwr.co.uk/</a></p> <p>The HORSE PWR site is designed to open the doors to the sport and talk about the Thoroughbred horse – their purpose, the lives they lead, and the high welfare and safety standards that underpin British racing.   We want to provide facts, educate, and confront the tough questions head on. The facts matter. Why? Because we understand our responsibility for our horses.</p> <p> </p> <p> </p> <p><!--Future Ticketing API - START--><br /> <script type='text/javascript' src='https://embed.futureticketing.ie/ft6141a3569515b'></script><br /> <script type='text/javascript'>var FTicket = FT({FT_event:'96'});</script><br /> <!--Future Ticketing API - END--></p>

observations.title: Richie and Mario, Stories and Songs – an Acoustic Way of Life
observations.description:
Owner Mario Lapointe will join local musician Richie Gallacher for a gig raising funds for Tullochan and DFC next month.
Get your tickets on FanBase
After the success of last year’s event, Richie and Mario, Stories and Songs – an Acoustic Way of Life, will see the duo entertain guests with tales from their lives, as well as acoustic performances in The Rock on Friday September 25.
All the money raised from ticket sales will be donated to Tullochan, based on Poplar Road, a youth development charity who work with over 1000 young people each year between the ages of 5 and 25.
Tullochan offers a range of bespoke programmes within primary and secondary schools, as well as tailored support through the Tullochan Training Academy, including work placement opportunities, personal development programmes and drop-in groups.
Mario, who performs under the stage name Vintage Lapointe and has had his work streamed more than 1m times online, said: “Last year’s event was very emotional for me. Especially so soon after buying the club and getting to know people in Dumbarton. I don’t perform in front of people very often, but the feedback we got was amazing and it was such a powerful experience.
“Both Richie and I are passionate about music, sport and using these to support young people. And it was an honour to share a stage with him. I’m really looking forward to doing it again, especially without all the nerves of performing live in Scotland for the first time like last year.
“Last year I also got to see the life-changing work that Tullochan is doing across Dumbarton and the region, and it’s something we’re incredibly proud to support.
“It will be a night of original music where Richie and I will talk about the stories and emotions behind each song.
“It kicks off a big weekend for the whole town with both our men’s and women’s team having home games, and with the Dumbarton Rocks Festival. Which will be the biggest ever!”
Richie added: “After 11 years at Tullochan, including four-and-a-half as CEO, I made the difficult decision to move on this year. The charity is in excellent hands with Amanda Black, and I’ll always feel connected to the team and the impact they deliver for young people and families.
“With rising costs and reduced funding across the third sector, every donation helps Tullochan stay responsive and continue supporting young people to build confidence and skills for a positive future.
“I’m looking forward to playing again with Mario, last year’s gig was great, and this one will be even better.”
Tickets are on sale now via Fanbase priced at £10, with doors opening from 6.30pm on Friday September 25.

observations.title: CreativeMornings/Cardiff | CURRENT + Bethan Elfyn for Cardiff Music City Festival
observations.description:
For this month’s theme let’s ride the crest of the radio waves, and learn a bit about radio and Welsh broadcasting history! We’re please to announce a talk and interview with Bethan Elfyn, spanning a three decade career at the BBC. ‘Currently’ a Senior Content Producer running the Horizons / Gorwelion music project (a partnership between BBC Wales and the Arts Council) and new music presenter on BBC Radio Wales. Well known as event curator, champion, festival host and being the first Welsh female host on BBC Radio One.
Marconi, 90s Wales nostalgia, and where radio and music are at now will lead the conversation between Bethan and BBC colleague, Horizons’ producer, former S4C music host, Leni Hatcher.
We’ll end the session with a curated playlist of new music, working with the theme!
